text: #788, under its ratified plan: a Vitest or Jest TypeScript precheck that refuses an acceptance test now says why. The refusal lists every diagnostic with its TS code, part-relative file, one-based line and column when there is one, and its complete flattened message, chains included, and says so when a diagnostic has no source location. The authenticated parent sends them as diagnostic events, chunked within the 4096-byte frame limit, only right after begin and before its own refusal, so they explain a refusal and never count as evidence. The factory's comment keeps every line that fits its size limit. Planning instructions and docs/factory.md now teach how to test a module the plan creates: relative imports, a string-typed dynamic import specifier, a locally declared API type, and loading asserted inside the selected test. The attribution rules are unchanged.
